title: Same-host Crawler
summary: Traverse a web graph in breadth-first order while enforcing same-host and duplicate-visit invariants.

clarifyingQuestions: Should trailing slashes and redirects be normalized? (Fragments and query strings stay part of the visit key for this problem.)
Should failed fetches be retried, skipped, or returned separately?
Does deterministic order still matter if worker fanout is added later?
followUps: Add worker fanout with a lock around the URL claim point.
Add a per-host rate limiter before each fetch.
Add cancellation with a threading.Event checked before enqueue and before fetch.
followUpGuide: For worker fanout, keep the queue shared but make URL claiming atomic. Hold a lock only while checking and adding to `visited`, then release it before calling `get_links`.

For cancellation, pass a `threading.Event` into workers and check it before dequeue, before fetch, and before enqueue. Use timed queue waits and bounded fetch timeouts too: an event alone can't interrupt a worker blocked inside `get_links`.
For rate limiting, put a per-host limiter before fetch. Since this problem enforces one host, a single limiter is enough; generalized crawlers should key the limiter by parsed host.
complexityAnalysis: - Naive DFS approach: recursively follow links and filter after traversal. Time: O(V + E) on reachable pages but may waste work on off-host edges. Space: O(V) for visited plus recursion depth.
- Recommended BFS approach: claim each same-host URL before enqueueing. Time: O(V + E). Space: O(V), where V is visited same-host URLs and E is inspected links.
- Worker follow-up: shared queue plus locked claim set keeps total work O(V + E). Space: O(V + W), where W is worker count.
solutionGuide: Use a FIFO queue for breadth-first traversal. Parse the start URL once for its exact netloc, seed the queue with the start URL as-is, then accept only discovered candidates with HTTP(S) schemes and that netloc. Keep fragments and query strings; reject resolved candidates that contain whitespace or fail parsing with ValueError.
The important invariant is: a URL enters the queue only after it has been accepted into `visited`. In threaded follow-ups, protect that claim step with a lock and fetch outside the lock.

Complexity is O(V + E) over visited pages and inspected links when URL lengths are bounded. For variable-length URLs, add the total characters scanned during resolution, parsing, whitespace checks, and hashing; storage also includes the strings in visited and the queue.
